subject: schema-27 run-scoped delegation record and delegated write/revoke boundary
source_of_truth: PostgreSQL work_run_delegation owner row and same-transaction evidence/session-note/idempotency rows
initial_state: Schema 27 is installed in a guarded disposable PostgreSQL database.
The parent owns one unsettled run and one active creator instance.
The parent identity has matching principal/workspace/client/grant binding and work:evidence authority.
No live delegation exists for the run before mint; tokens and DSNs are not packet data.

operations.name: mint two delegations with distinct idempotency keys for the same run
operations.synchronization: Two independent PostgreSQL connections start at a barrier before mint.

operations.name: write one session note using a resolved delegated context
operations.synchronization: A test wrapper pauses after owner row FOR SHARE succeeds and before the note insert.

operations.name: revoke the delegation while the delegated note write is paused
operations.synchronization: A separate connection invokes revoke; pg_blocking_pids confirms it waits on the writer transaction.

operations.name: retry a note write with the cached delegated context after revoke commits
operations.synchronization: Invoke only after the owner revoke response has committed.

operations.name: resolve a token after expiry or revocation and inspect the persisted credential digest
operations.synchronization: Use the owner database clock and query only the digest column plus redacted idempotency result.

consistency.object: one live delegation per exact run; shared delegated-write lock serializes before exclusive revoke; no write after revoke commit

assumptions.isolation: PostgreSQL default READ COMMITTED; each write and revoke uses one owner transaction.
assumptions.clock: Owner expiry comparisons use the PostgreSQL owner clock; one test-only clock hook is frozen inside the disposable database.
assumptions.fairness: The paused writer is explicitly released after PostgreSQL reports the revoke blocked on its lock.

invariants: At most one unrevoked and unexpired delegation exists for a run; a two-mint race has one success and one delegation-exists refusal.
A delegated operation is bound to the owner-resolved exact run and one of the closed operation allowlist.
A delegated write whose shared row lock precedes revoke may commit first; revoke waits for it, and a subsequent cached-context write refuses without adding a note.
Persisted credentials are plain SHA-256 digests; an exact mint retry returns no token and the idempotency record contains no token.
A child expiry is no later than a supplied trusted parent expiry or the owner-clock TTL cap.
oracles: Complete actual PostgreSQL suite passes on the guarded disposable database.
